sample_unit: LLMs trained (1.3B and 4B parameter) with simulated poisoning of The Pile

links.outcome: Whether public medical benchmark scores reveal poisoned-model harms
links.effect: Corrupted models matched corruption-free counterparts on open-source medical benchmarks routinely used to evaluate medical LLMs, despite producing more medical errors.
links.quote: Furthermore, we discover that corrupted models match the performance of their corruption-free counterparts on open-source benchmarks routinely used to evaluate medical LLMs.

links.outcome: Vulnerability of LLMs to training-data poisoning with medical misinformation
links.effect: Replacing just 0.001% of training tokens with medical misinformation produced harmful models more likely to propagate medical errors.
links.quote: We find that replacement of just 0.001% of training tokens with medical misinformation results in harmful models more likely to propagate medical errors.

links.outcome: Share of harmful LLM output captured by knowledge-graph screening
links.effect: Knowledge-graph screening captured 91.9% of harmful content (F1 = 85.7%).
links.quote: Using biomedical knowledge graphs to screen medical LLM outputs, we propose a harm mitigation strategy that captures 91.9% of harmful content (F1 = 85.7%).

unlisted_practices: Screening LLM outputs against biomedical knowledge graphs
Improved data provenance and vetting of web-scraped LLM training data

screen.reason: Empirical study testing vulnerability of medical LLMs to data-poisoning attacks and evaluating a harm-mitigation guardrail (biomedical knowledge graph output screening) to catch harmful outputs.
